# Comprehensive Characterization of Concept Drifts in Process Mining written by Alexander Kraus
 ## About Repository This repository contains the prototype of the approach and details on the data collection, experiment configurations, and raw results presented in (paper under review) *Alexander Kraus, Han van der Aa (2023). 'Comprehensive Characterization of Concept Drifts in Process Mining.'
* ## About Research ### Context Business processes are subject to frequent changes due to the dynamic environments in which they are executed. Analyzing data recorded during the execution of such changing processes results in the presence of concept drifts, i.e., situations in which an event log contains data from different versions of a process. Concept drift detection aims to avoid the detrimental impact that such concept drifts can have on obtained process mining results by detecting when drifts occurred, localizing modifications, and understanding how drifts manifest over time. This paper focuses on the latter task, i.e., drift characterization, which seeks to understand whether changes unfolded suddenly or gradually and if they form complex patterns like incremental or recurring drifts ### Problem However, current solutions for automatically detecting concept drifts in event logs lack comprehensive characterization capabilities. Instead, they mainly focus on drift detection and characterization of isolated process changes. This leads to an incomplete understanding of more complex concept drifts, like incremental and recurring drifts, when several process changes are inter-connected. ### Solution This paper overcomes such limitations by introducing an improved taxonomy for characterizing concept drifts and a three-step framework that provides an automatic characterization of concept drifts in event logs. We evaluated our framework through elaborate evaluation experiments conducted using a large collection of synthetic event logs. The results highlight the effectiveness and accuracy of our proposed framework and show that it outperforms state-of-the-art techniques. ![Overview of the main steps of our framework](/evaluation_paper/framework_overview.png) ## Setup and Usage ### Installation instructions The following steps provide instructions on how to install and run the approach (check the 'configuration.py' file in the folder 'package': 1. Upgrade your python version to >= 3.11 or later (the project was built and tested with python 3.11) 2. Create a virtual environment for the project (optional) 3. Install the dependencies in 'requirements.txt' using pip command: pip install -r requirements.txt ## Directories The following default directories are used by the approach: * DEFAULT_INPUT_DIR = 'input/', is used as a general input folder for the event logs in xes-format for the main script * DEFAULT_OUTPUT_DIR = 'output/', is used as an output folder for any approach execution ## Usage The next steps describe how to apply the approach: 1. Place your event log in xes-format into the DEFAULT_INPUT_DIR 2. Configure the parameter settings in project_packages/configurations.py (if needed) 3. Run the project using python main.py ## Evaluation To evaluate our work, we used [CDLG tool](https://gitlab.uni-mannheim.de/processanalytics/cdlg_tool) to generate a dataset consisting of 100 event logs, with each log containing between one and three drifts, of different types. Using the [CDLG input paramter file](evaluation_paper/data_collection/CDLG_parameter_file), we generated a collection of 100 event logs. The 100 event logs contain a total of 198 drifts, with simple sudden and gradual drifts involving a single process change and complex recurring and incremental drifts comprising three process changes, resulting in a total of 426 process changes. Each process change can occur suddenly, resulting in a single change point, or gradually, resulting in two change points (gradual start and end), leading to 651 change points in total. The evaluation results are stored in the folder ['evaluation_paper'](evaluation_paper/). ## Reproducibility To obtain our evaluation results for Steps 2 and 3: 1. Unpack the zipped event logs in the folder 'evaluation_paper/data_collection/datasets_evaluation' 2. Set the parameter DEFAULT_INPUT_DIR in the file 'packages/configurations.py' to the path in Step 1 3. Run the project using python main.py [arg] to obtain evaluation results, setting 'arg' to: - 'approach_step_3' to obtain results for Step 3 (Steps 1 and 2 use gold standard) - 'approach_steps_2_3' to obtain results for Steps 2 and 3 (Step 1 uses gold standard) - 'approach' to obtain end-to-end results 4. Run the 'evaluate.py' and 'evaluate_grouped' scripts from the folder 'evaluation_paper/' to get evaluation results To replicate results for Step 1, repeat the steps above for other change point detection techniques, replace the value 'process_graphs' in parameter 'STEP1' ('packages/configurations.py') with one of the following options: 'emd', 'prodrift', 'zheng', 'bose_j', 'process_graphs', 'lcdd', 'adwin_j'. ## References * [PM4PY](https://pm4py.fit.fraunhofer.de) * [Concept Drift Evaluation Framework](https://github.com/cpitsch/cdrift-evaluation/) * [CDLG tool](https://gitlab.uni-mannheim.de/processanalytics/cdlg_tool)
